The regression is fixed.

## What was wrong

`site/css/tokens.css` declared the bundled web font with a single weight:

```css
@font-face {
  src: url('../fonts/acme-sans.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-weight: 400;   /* ← pinned the whole font to the 400 instance */
}
```

`acme-sans.woff2` is actually a **variable font** (a renamed Figtree with a `wght` axis of 300–900 — confirmed by its `fvar`/`STAT`/`HVAR` tables). Declaring `font-weight: 400` told the browser that the file only covers weight 400, so every bold weight (headings at 800, nav/brand/buttons at 600–700) fell back to synthetic emboldening of the 400 outlines instead of using the real bold instances.

That's why only bold text looked wrong — I measured brand text at 136 px now vs. 141 px in the baselines, identical across every weight. Body text at 400 was unaffected, which matches the diff regions (headings, nav links, brand, buttons — no body copy).

## Fix

```css
font-weight: 300 900;
```

This lets the browser select real instances across the variable axis.

## Verification

- `tests/visual.spec.ts`: **12/12 passed, 0 changed, 0 missing** (desktop + phone, all six pages)
- `tests/functional.spec.ts`: **16/16 passed**

Only `site/css/tokens.css` was modified; no baselines were approved or changed.
